webJournal.title: Web Journal
webJournal.subtitle: Product updates, engineering notes and what the team is thinking about.

custody.title: How we think about insured custody
custody.excerpt: Where your keys live, who can touch them, and what our insurance actually covers.
custody.body1: Insured custody means two separate things, and they get conflated. The first is where the private keys physically live: in our case, split across hardware modules that no single employee can reach alone. The second is what happens if that fails.
custody.body2: Our policy covers loss from external breach and internal misuse, up to the stated limit. It does not cover a compromise of your own device or credentials, which is why 2FA is mandatory on withdrawals rather than optional.

fees.title: A flat 0.10% spot fee, explained
fees.excerpt: Why we moved to a single spot fee and what it means for high-volume accounts.
fees.body1: A flat 0.10% spot fee replaced a tiered schedule that almost nobody could predict. The old model rewarded volume, but it also meant the number on your confirmation screen depended on where the month had landed.
fees.body2: For high-volume accounts the flat rate is slightly worse on paper. In practice the certainty turned out to be worth more than the rebate — most of the desks we spoke to were pricing in the worst tier anyway.

kycFlow.title: Rebuilding KYC to take under two minutes
kycFlow.excerpt: The old flow lost people at document upload. Here is what we changed.
kycFlow.body1: Document upload was where the old flow lost people. Roughly a third of them stopped at that step, most on a phone, most after the second failed capture attempt.
kycFlow.body2: So we moved the capture guidance to before the camera opens, accepted a wider range of image quality, and pushed the checks that used to block submission into the background. The median completion time is now under two minutes.

roadmap.title: What is shipping next
roadmap.excerpt: Peer-to-peer transfers, more networks per coin, and a redesigned wallet view.
roadmap.body1: Peer-to-peer transfers are the next thing to ship. The mechanics are in place; what remains is the dispute path, which we would rather get right than get out early.
roadmap.body2: After that: more networks per coin, and a wallet view rebuilt around holdings instead of accounts. The current screen made sense with three coins and stopped making sense at thirty.

networks.title: More networks for every coin
networks.excerpt: Choosing a network used to be guesswork. Each coin now lists the networks it actually supports, with fees attached.
networks.body1: Choosing a network used to be guesswork: the field accepted anything, and a wrong choice meant funds arriving somewhere unrecoverable. That is a bad way to learn how chains differ.
networks.body2: Each coin now lists only the networks it genuinely supports, with the fee and the expected settlement time attached to each. Anything unsupported is not selectable rather than a warning you can click past.

security.title: What 2FA does and does not protect
security.excerpt: Two-factor stops someone using a stolen password. Here is what still needs your attention, and why we ask for it on withdrawals.
security.body1: Two-factor authentication stops one specific thing well: someone who has your password using it. That is the most common attack by a wide margin, which is why it is on by default.
security.body2: What it does not stop is a compromise of the device holding the second factor, or your approving a transfer you were talked into. Withdrawals therefore carry a separate confirmation, and new addresses hold for a short window before the first send.

about.title: Built for people who want control of their crypto
about.intro: AdCrypto is a crypto wallet and exchange platform that lets people buy, sell, hold and move digital assets safely from a single dashboard.
about.missionText: Make managing multiple cryptocurrencies as simple as using a regular banking app, without giving up security or control over your funds.
about.visionText: A single trusted place to hold every coin you own, move it anywhere, and prove who you are only once.

security.title: Security first
security.text: KYC, 2FA and email verification are built in from day one, not bolted on later.

simplicity.title: Simple by default
simplicity.text: Buying, selling and exchanging crypto should take a few taps, not a manual.

transparency.title: Transparent activity
transparency.text: Every transaction is logged and visible to you, in real time.

aboutPanel.para1: AdCrypto started with a simple frustration: moving digital assets took too many apps, too many confirmations and too much guesswork. We rebuilt the flow end to end — verification, custody, settlement — so that holding crypto feels like holding money.
aboutPanel.para2: Today the platform serves hundreds of thousands of transactions a day across four major currencies and nine payment gateways, wrapped in eight layers of protection that never ask you to think about them.

bullets.custody: Fully-insured custody with role-based internal access
bullets.fees: No hidden fees — every cost shown before you confirm

faq.text: Still stuck? Our team answers in under an hour, every day of the week.

what.a: AdCrypto is a single wallet for buying, holding and moving digital assets. One account covers spot, futures and settlement, on Android, iOS and the web.

protection.a: Every account runs behind eight layers of protection — verification, 2FA, end-to-end encryption, role-based access, SSL and an application firewall among them.

currencies.a: Four majors are supported at launch for holding, swapping and settlement, with nine payment gateways to fund your balance.

fees.a: No. Network costs are shown before you confirm a transfer, and there are no withdrawal surprises or monthly account charges.

speed.a: Internal transfers land instantly. On-chain settlement typically confirms in under a second on the networks we support at peak throughput.

rewards.q: How do I claim the welcome rewards?
rewards.a: Create an account, complete verification and your deposit, spot and futures rewards unlock automatically — up to 8,800 USDT in total.

security.subtitle: Security is not one feature. It is eight overlapping layers, each covering what the others cannot.

smsEmail.title: SMS or Email Verification
smsEmail.text: Both email and SMS make for more secure authentication, and each has trade-offs — so you choose which one guards your account.

kyc.text: Identity checks that satisfy compliance without turning sign-up into paperwork. Verified once, in under two minutes.

encryption.title: End-to-end Encryption
encryption.text: Communication where only the people talking can read the messages. Not us, and not anyone who intercepts them.

behavior.title: Behaviour Monitoring
behavior.text: We learn how your account normally behaves, so a login or transfer that does not fit gets challenged before it settles.

ssl.text: TLS encryption on every request between you and AdCrypto, so nothing readable crosses the network in between.

waf.title: Web Application Firewall
waf.text: A WAF inspects and filters HTTP traffic reaching the platform, stopping known attack patterns before they touch the app.

rbac.title: Role-Based Access Control
rbac.text: Administrative access is scoped to roles and responsibilities, so no single person can reach everything.
